title: Small Implicit Graph Conjecture
formal: Does every hereditary small graph class \(\mathcal C\) admit an adjacency labeling scheme using at most \(K\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\) bits per vertex on every \(n\)-vertex graph in \(\mathcal C\), for some constant \(K\) depending only on \(\mathcal C\)?

source_formulation.text: However, it is still unknown if all such classes admit an implicit representation (see [12] for more details on implicit representation of small classes).
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 4

why: A short global description of every graph does not by itself make adjacency locally decodable from two short vertex descriptions. The conjecture asks whether a precise growth restriction and induced-subgraph closure suffice to bridge this gap.
status_note: The hereditary small conjecture is explicit in the 2024 source and repeated in the 2025 follow-up. The later abstract and algorithmic labeling definition were checked on 13 September 2026; no full logarithmic result was verified. Status is source_open.

progress.text: The source proves the monotone small case and states the hereditary extension as Conjecture 9.
The follow-up gives \(O((\log n)^3)\)-bit labels for hereditary small classes, and logarithmic labels under additional weak sparsity.

importance.reason: A named surviving implicit-representation conjecture that tests when global graph-class entropy supports logarithmic local labels.

sentences: An adjacency labeling scheme assigns each vertex a short binary string from which adjacency can be determined using only two labels.
The conjecture asks for logarithmic labels in every hereditary class with at most a factorial times a fixed exponential number of labeled graphs.
Hereditary means closed under induced subgraphs, and is weaker than closure under all subgraphs.
The monotone case is known, and a 2025 follow-up proves logarithmic-cubed labels for all hereditary small classes.
The question isolates when low total information content permits efficient storage in locally decodable vertex descriptions.

definitions: Graphs are finite, undirected and simple. A graph class \(\mathcal C\) is closed under isomorphism; it is hereditary when every induced subgraph of every member also belongs to it. Write \(\mathcal C_n\) for its members with labeled vertex set \([n]\). Small means that there is a constant \(c\geq1\) with \(|\mathcal C_n|\leq n!c^n\) for every \(n\geq1\). A labeling scheme consists of an encoder and a decoder, fixed for the class and all input lengths. The encoder, given an adjacency-matrix encoding of \(G\in\mathcal C_n\), assigns one finite binary label to each vertex. The decoder receives only two labels and returns whether the corresponding distinct vertices are adjacent; it receives no graph description, class-membership oracle, additional table or external value of \(n\). Any size information needed by the decoder must be encoded within the labels. Both are deterministic algorithms, with no imposed time bound; encoding must halt on every graph in the class and decoding must halt on every pair of finite labels. Outside-class encoder behavior is unrestricted. All answers for pairs of vertices of an input member must be exact and simultaneous. Label length is the sole resource being bounded. No polynomial-time recognition of the class is assumed. Monotone, which is a stronger condition, means closed under deletion of both vertices and edges; this question assumes only hereditary closure.

context_blocks.text: The saved source proves logarithmic adjacency labels for monotone small classes and explicitly conjectures the extension to hereditary small classes. Its Conjecture 9 is the Small Implicit Graph Conjecture. The earlier draft title incorrectly described the already-treated monotone case.

The broader conjecture for all hereditary classes of factorial growth is false. The sharper small-class bound limits the number of labeled graphs to a factorial times a fixed exponential, leaving a distinct question.

The 2025 follow-up proves \(O((\log n)^3)\)-bit labels for every hereditary small class and logarithmic labels for small weakly sparse classes. Weak sparsity means excluding some fixed complete bipartite graph as a subgraph; that additional restriction is absent in the general conjecture.

answer_criterion: Provide a complete Lean-checked proof of a labeling scheme and a class-dependent logarithmic length constant for every hereditary small class, or exhibit such a class and prove that no scheme satisfying these conditions exists. No efficient encoding or decoding time is required beyond the source’s algorithmic definition. A result for monotone or weakly sparse classes alone does not settle the universal claim.

notes: Replaced the misleading monotone title by the established conjecture name and recovered the hereditary small target from the saved summary and Conjecture 9.

Specified labeled growth, a single class-dependent encoder/decoder, local exact decoding and no unstated efficiency requirement; did not replace algorithms with arbitrary noncomputable universal-graph sequences.
Added the 2025 logarithmic-cubed improvement and weakly sparse special case; neither is the full logarithmic conjecture.
